answer_text:
The Littlewood–Richardson coefficient \(C^{(2,1)}_{(1),(1,1)}\) counts the number of Littlewood–Richardson tableaux of skew shape

\[
(2,1)/(1,1)
\]

with content \((1)\).

The partition \((2,1)\) has diagram

\[
\begin{array}{cc}
\square & \square \\
\square &
\end{array}
\]

and the inner partition \((1,1)\) occupies the leftmost column:

\[
\begin{array}{cc}
\square & \\
\square &
\end{array}
\]

So the skew shape \((2,1)/(1,1)\) consists of exactly one box:

\[
\begin{array}{cc}
 & \square \\
 &
\end{array}
\]

We must fill this one box with the content \((1)\), meaning we place a single \(1\). The resulting tableau is

\[
\begin{array}{cc}
 & 1 \\
 &
\end{array}
\]

This is a valid Littlewood–Richardson tableau, and there is only one such filling.

Therefore,

\[
C^{(2,1)}_{(1),(1,1)} = 1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
